title: Mandela says he fought white domination and black domination
summary: Mandela says he fought both white domination and black domination.
body: Mandela's speech, as Fordham prints it, says he has fought against white domination and against black domination, and that he has cherished a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony. The speech is his statement. It is not Geyer's 1953 case. The wording on the page includes: "go to my own words during my trial in 1964 - they are as true today as they were then: I have fought against white domination, and I have fought against black domination. I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunity. It is an ideal which I hope to live for and to achieve. But, if need be, it is an ideal for which I am prepared to die.". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
